harmonicFunction: Am (i) - Heavy, moody minor tonic establishing intense emotional urgency
G (♭VII) - Mixolydian subtonic creating forward rock momentum and vocal release
F (♭VI) - Dramatic submediant chord delivering maximum emotional tension in the Aeolian cadence
E7 (V7) - Harmonic minor dominant providing classical leading-tone resolution in the acoustic intro

techniques.name: Flamenco-Style Acoustic Pull-Offs & High-Speed Strumming
techniques.description: Executing Nancy Wilson's virtuosic acoustic introduction featuring lightning-fast pull-offs on the B and G strings, rapid strumming rasgueado accents, and seamless transitions into electric power chords

notes: Silver Wheels pull-off flurry: Rapid sixteenth notes pulling off from C (fret 1 B) to open B and open G
Acoustic attack: Nancy Wilson uses a flatpick combined with fingers (hybrid picking) on an acoustic dreadnought
Electric bridge transition: Heavy downstroke palm muting on the low E string locking with the kick drum at 130 BPM
sequence: Master the finger agility for the open B string pull-off pattern at 90 BPM
Build metronome speed on the acoustic prelude up to performance tempo of 130 BPM
Practice the dramatic sudden switch from acoustic fingerstyle to aggressive electric chugging
Execute the full Aeolian power chord cadence (Am - G - F - G) with tight rhythmic punch
tips: Use a heavy gauge acoustic pick (0.88mm to 1.0mm) to get a loud, crisp, cutting acoustic percussive attack
Keep your left-hand knuckles parallel to the fretboard to maintain rapid pull-off speed without touching adjacent strings
Do not rush the transition out of the intro—give the final E7 arpeggio full dramatic space before the electric guitars explode

beginner.title: Aeolian Chords & Electric Power Grooves
steps: Learn the root-5 and root-6 power chords for A5, G5, and F5
Practice downstroke strumming locked to 130 BPM with a metronome
Master the chorus progression (F - G - Am) with smooth transitions

intermediate.title: Acoustic Prelude Pull-Off Flurry
steps: Practice the 16th-note pull-off pattern between fret 1 and open B string slowly at 80 BPM
Develop finger independence between fretting index finger and open-string pull-offs
Increase speed gradually while keeping pull-offs loud and even in volume

advanced.title: Virtuosic Prelude Performance & Electric Solos
steps: Perform Nancy Wilson's complete 'Silver Wheels' prelude at full 130 BPM tempo without stumbling
Execute Roger Fisher's high-register screaming blues bends and unison double stops
Combine acoustic dexterity with hard-rock swagger in a full band live performance

commonMistakes: Collapsing the left-hand index finger during acoustic pull-offs, muting adjacent ringing strings
Rushing ahead of the 130 BPM beat during the excitement of the acoustic intro flurry
Failing to mute the low E string when playing the A5 power chord, causing muddy dissonance
practiceRoutine: 10 minutes: Left-hand pull-off stamina drills on the B and G strings at 90-120 BPM
15 minutes: Nancy Wilson acoustic prelude run-throughs with digital metronome
15 minutes: Downstroke power chord rhythm tightening over the verse and chorus tracks
focusAreas: Acoustic pull-off volume balance and clarity
Right-hand pick accuracy on the acoustic flurry
Seamless dynamic explosion into the electric band arrangement
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 130 BPM with sixteenth-note clicks and practice playing 4 clean pull-offs per beat in the intro
